source_read: PMC full text PMC5944879 (Am J Public Health 2018;108(6):777–781) in my own browser tab (title checked): abstract, untitled Introduction, METHODS, RESULTS, Tables 1–3 (rendered as text; every percentage and the Table 3 sums recomputed, Wald intervals checked for the Total, 2012, Hispanic and Hispanic-male rows), DISCUSSION with Limitations, Public Health Implications, Human Participant Protection, author information and the CONTRIBUTORS note (collapsed panels read with javascript on my tab), and all 13 references. No funding, conflict-of-interest or acknowledgment section exists on the page. For the card's statements about the linked editorial, only its passages naming this study were read (Galea and Vaughan, PMC5944893, doi 10.2105/AJPH.2018.304422). Card check only (task has no claims; step 1 empty).

design.note: Comparison of two case definitions applied to the same statewide medical-examiner records; descriptive only.

instrument.note: JBI prevalence, as for the other certificate studies in this round (see my note on buchanich_2018 about METHODS 5.3 listing registry descriptions under no instrument).

key_findings.note: RESULTS, 1st paragraph (the text rounds 28.6% to 'approximately 29%'); Table 1 Total row. Recomputed 1,130/3,957 = 28.6%, 2,182/3,957 = 55.1%, 2,182/1,130 = 1.93.
Table 1: all eight yearly percentages recompute; the year columns sum to 3,957, 1,130 and 2,182.
RESULTS, 2nd and 4th paragraphs; 804 + 193 + 55 = 1,052; 76.4%, 18.3%, 5.2% recompute. The Limitations describe the 55 as naming a substance other than heroin or morphine.
Table 3: 1,130/2,182 = 51.8%, CI 49.7–53.9 reproduced; year and age rows recompute; age totals sum to 2,181 and age-row standard counts to 1,130.
Table 3; all race, gender and race-by-gender rows recompute, and the race-by-gender rows add up to the race rows.
DISCUSSION › Limitations, single paragraph; the authors also conclude the enhanced count 'almost certainly' is more accurate.
DISCUSSION, 7th paragraph. The paragraph's citation is ref 12 (the 2015 Maryland Vital Statistics Annual Report), not the SAMHSA panel paper (ref 10); see missed.

reporting_issues.note: Table 2 prints 1,042; the text gives 804 in both the 2nd and 4th paragraphs of RESULTS.
Abstract › Results names 'the presence of morphine, either alone or in combination with quinine' as a major factor.
Ref 7 is the state report on drug- and alcohol-related intoxication deaths. 1,052/3,957 = 26.6%.
Checked: the page has only a CONTRIBUTORS note, Human Participant Protection and Footnotes; there is no funding, acknowledgment or conflict section.

risk_of_bias.note: Moderate (editors' summary; JBI has no overall algorithm). This is consistent with the difference from buchanich_2018: here each added death rests on that death's own toxicology or scene record, not on an assumed proportion. The protocol, however, is unvalidated, partly presence-based, and was applied by the producing agencies with reviewers not reported. Item 8 checked: the intervals are Wald-type and reproduce.

interpretation_gap.note: Minor. Gap (5) checked: the editorial's passages naming this study summarize it as showing that standard certificates may underestimate heroin deaths and that enhanced surveillance can better identify heroin, with no comment on the method.

missed: Reporting issue: the SAMHSA recommendations in DISCUSSION, 7th paragraph (list every physiologically significant drug, name the parent drug rather than the metabolite, avoid 'overdose' and 'use', judge whether toxicology separates chronic from acute use) are cited to ref 12, the 2015 Maryland Vital Statistics Annual Report. The SAMHSA panel paper is ref 10. The card's replication timeline says this recommendation is cited as ref 10. Correct it to 'printed as ref 12, presumably meant ref 10'.

RESULTS, 3rd paragraph calls the Table 3 figures 'the percentage of overdose death records reporting heroin'. They are the share of protocol-defined heroin deaths whose certificate named heroin, a sensitivity against the enhanced definition, not a share of all overdose deaths. The card's findings word this correctly; the paper's wording should not be copied into claims.

DISCUSSION, 8th paragraph links the rise from 45.7% (2012) to 56.3% (2015) to implementation of these recommendations being under way in Maryland, but gives no data on implementation. This is a trend read as an effect.

Addition to funding.affiliations_note: by the CONTRIBUTORS note, Fowler (the chief medical examiner) contributed to data collection and to the study's conception and design, and Horon to data collection, analysis and interpretation. So the certifying office helped both build and apply the protocol.

Correction (cannot_establish): 'no independent reference standard or second reviewer was used'. The paper does not report who reviewed the records or how many reviewers there were, so 'second reviewer not reported' is accurate. The card's exposure field already words it that way.
